judgment.delivery_claim_why: It says each session or subagent request receives the rules for the model it runs on, explicitly 'delivery, not obedience', with no claim of enforcement or perfect delivery and a correctly stated measurement (299 sessions, Claude Code 2.1.330).

reasons.reason: It fits a setup with four models and many subagents
reasons.why: The reference says nothing about the docs' advice on when to skip it or about the team's setup.

reasons.reason: Its edge over CLAUDE.md is in subagents: 448/448 main, 60/128 subagents for CLAUDE.md vs 763/763
reasons.why: Matches D34, D28 and D20 and the reference's L10.

reasons.reason: It sends each model less irrelevant text: 78.6% vs 32.6%, 1,343 vs 4,472 chars
Evidence of better results is thin: 133/132/133 of 144, pilot delivered to main conversation only
reasons.why: Matches B1 and the pilot description.

reasons.reason: Only a few rules have a measured effect on small tasks (verify-changes, Sonnet carry-through, Fable low-context-report; Haiku carry-through nothing; cost about double; 600/600 passed)
reasons.why: Matches R3, R5 to R11 and R14.

reasons.reason: Out of the box it does little for Opus and Fable since their attended rules ship off
It is very young: not on npm, installed from a clone, nine failures F1-F9 found and fixed
reasons.why: Matches L7 and L5; the version and changelog details are not contradicted.

reasons.reason: Operational risk is low: hooks never block, no network except classifier, no runtime dependencies, uninstall and report available
reasons.why: The reference lists no blocking, no network except the classifier, no runtime dependencies, and the uninstall and report commands.
